text:
liz (support): Heads-up: we're getting >10 customer pings about the console hourly usage graphs being ~4-6 hours behind for a bunch of tenants. First reports came in ~03:10 UTC. :eyes:
rahul (eng-data): looking now. quick check: consumer group 'usage-hourly-consumer' shows sustained lag on partition ranges.
meera (ingest): ingest-bot raised S3 read error alerts at 03:05 for prefix s3://redwood-usage/2026-03-15/. Noticed a spike in 5xx when workers tried to read manifest files.
ingest-bot: alert: s3-read-errors >= 20 in 5m for prefix s3://redwood-usage/2026-03-15/ (first_seen=2026-03-15T03:05:12Z).
rahul (eng-data): reproducing consumer lag: `kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --group usage-hourly-consumer --describe` shows LAG ~1.2M for topic `usage_hourly_v2`.
sam (sre): timeline? did something deploy around 03:00?
dave (eng-infra): no infra deploys in that window, but we had an autoscaler bump on the ingest workers at 02:58 (scale-out triggered). logs show workers restarted quickly.
meera (ingest): running a quick grep on worker logs, saw repeated stack traces reading manifests: ```
ERROR ManifestLoader: Failed to fetch s3://redwood-usage/2026-03-15/manifest-0001.json -> 502 Bad Gateway
Trace: com.amazonaws.SdkClientException: Unable to execute HTTP request
```
rahul (eng-data): that would cause the consumer to ack later / requeue. looks like manifests stuck -> downstream aggregation skipped hours. which tenants affected?
liz (support): customers reporting: Acme, NimblePay, and a group of small tenants (IDs start with t-12*).
meera (ingest): quick query against raw manifest processing table shows ~07:30-08:00 UTC rows failed to process and got requeued. backfill job is currently pending.
sam (sre): I increased the ingest worker concurrency from 4 -> 8 to try to clear the backlog, and temporarily raised retry delay from 30s -> 5s to avoid long backoff. watching consumer lag. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
rahul (eng-data): ran a dry-run of the aggregate job for tenant Acme; missing points correspond exactly to manifests with read failures. If we reprocess those manifests, charts should fill in.
dave (eng-infra): investigating S3 proxy/gateway (we had transient errors to that endpoint). infra is seeing 502s from the cloud edge for the bucket region between 03:00-03:10 UTC. deploying a route failover for that region now.
meera (ingest): plan: 1) manual requeue of failed manifests for affected window (03:00-04:30) 2) kick a targeted backfill for top affected tenants 3) monitor dashboard ingestion metrics and consumer lag. running `scripts/requeue_manifests.sh --start 2026-03-15T03:00Z --end 2026-03-15T04:30Z` now.
liz (support): can we get an ETA to tell customers? they want an estimate for when charts will show backfilled hours.
sam (sre): if manual requeue + increased concurrency holds, estimate ~90-150 minutes to clear backlog for top-tier tenants (Acme/NimblePay). smaller tenants may be faster.
rahul (eng-data): following up: after requeue start, consumer lag dropped 20% in 10m. some manifests still fail intermittently (502). I'll add an exclusion to route those specific manifest keys to a retry queue with exponential backoff so we don't hammer S3 during edge flaps.
dave (eng-infra): failover to secondary S3 edge completed at 03:25 UTC. 502 rate has dropped to baseline.
meera (ingest): requeue finished for the window; kicked targeted backfill for the top 50 tenants. first batches completing, aggregation worker output shows hourly rows being written again.
liz (support): updated customers: told Acme/NimblePay ETA ~2hrs, mentioned root cause = transient S3 edge 502s causing manifest read failures and consumer backlog. they asked for postmortem once done.
rahul (eng-data): created follow-up ticket: INC-6791 to track permanent mitigation (improve manifest read retries, route diversity, and backoff tuning). assigned to eng-data + eng-infra.
sam (sre): monitoring consumer lag, now within acceptable window for priority tenants. leaving autoscaler adjustments for later.
liz (support): thanks all. I will close this thread once dashboards show stable data for 6 hours backfill window. please ping if ETA changes. :thumbsup:
